translations.text: The Lord called Moses and spoke to him from inside the tent of meeting, saying:
“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: If anyone among you brings an offering to the Lord, you shall bring your offering from the livestock, from the cattle or from the flock.
If his offering is a burnt offering from the cattle, he shall bring a male without blemish. He shall bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting as an acceptable gift before the Lord.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the animal he has brought for a burnt offering, so that it may be accepted for him and he may be forgiven on its account.
They shall slaughter the bull before the Lord. Aaron’s sons, the priests themselves, shall bring its blood and pour the blood all around the altar at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
They shall skin it and cut it into its separate parts.
Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall put fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.
Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall arrange the pieces they have cut, together with the head and the fat, on the wood over the fire on the altar.
They shall wash its entrails and legs with water, and the priest shall place all of it on the altar. It is a sacrificial offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
If his offering to the Lord is from the flock, whether a sheep or a goat, he shall bring a male without blemish for a burnt offering.
They shall slaughter it on the north side of the altar before the Lord, and Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall pour its blood all around the altar.
They shall cut it into its separate parts, including its head and its fat, and the priests shall arrange them on the wood over the fire on the altar.
They shall wash its entrails and legs with water. The priest shall bring all of it and place it on the altar. It is a sacrificial offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
If he brings his sacrificial offering to the Lord from among the birds, he shall bring his offering from either turtledoves or pigeons.
The priest shall bring it to the altar, cut through its neck, and place it on the altar. He shall drain its blood at the base of the altar.
He shall remove its entrails together with its feathers and take them out toward the east, to the place where the ashes are deposited.
He shall tear it open by its wings but shall not divide it. The priest shall place it on the altar, on the wood over the fire. It is a sacrificial offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
If he brings an offering and sacrifice to the Lord in place of a life, his offering shall be fine flour. He shall pour oil over it and put frankincense on it. It is a sacrifice.

He shall take it to the sons of Aaron the priest. He shall take a handful of the fine flour with its oil and all its frankincense, and the priest shall place it on the altar as its memorial portion. It is a sacrifice with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
What remains of the offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It is a most holy portion of the offerings to the Lord.
If you bring an offering baked in an oven as a grain offering, it shall be unleavened loaves of fine flour mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers spread with oil.
If your offering is a sacrifice prepared on a griddle, it shall be fine flour mixed with oil and unleavened.
You shall break it into pieces and pour oil over the broken pieces. It is a sacrifice to the Lord.
If your grain offering is cooked in a pan, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.
You shall bring to the Lord the offering you have prepared from these things, and you shall bring it to the priest.
He shall bring it near the altar. The priest shall take the memorial portion from the offering, and the priest shall place it on the altar. It is a sacrifice, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
What remains of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy portion of the offerings to the Lord.
You shall not make anything that you bring as a burnt offering to the Lord with leaven. You shall not bring any leaven or any honey as a burnt offering to the Lord.
But you may bring some of it to the Lord as tithes, for you shall not sacrifice any of it on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.”
Every sacrificial offering of yours shall be prepared with salt. Salt must not be left out of what you sacrifice to the Lord. You shall put salt in all your offerings.
If you bring the Lord an offering from the firstfruits of your grain, you shall bring fresh grain, roasted, cleaned and crushed, as your offering from the firstfruits of your grain.
You shall pour oil on it and put frankincense on it. It is a grain offering.
The priest shall offer the memorial portion of that grain, together with its oil and all its frankincense. It is an offering to the Lord.
If his offering to the Lord is a sacrifice of well-being, and he brings it from the cattle, whether male or female, he shall bring an animal without blemish before the Lord.
He shall lay his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it at the entrance to the tent of testimony. Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall pour its blood on the altar.
From the sacrifice of well-being they shall present an offering to the Lord: the fat covering its belly and all the fat inside its belly;
and both its kidneys and the fat on them at the flanks. He shall remove the smaller lobe of the liver along with the kidneys.
Aaron’s sons shall offer these on the altar, on top of the offerings, on the wood that is on the fire, as an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
If his offering is from the flock, as a sacrifice of well-being to the Lord, he shall bring an animal without blemish, whether male or female.
If his offering is a lamb, he shall bring it before the Lord.
He shall lay his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it at the entrance to the tent of testimony. Aaron’s sons shall pour its blood all around the altar.

From the sacrifice of well-being he shall take an offering for the Lord: the fat and the whole fat tail, which he shall cut off together with the backbone, all the fat covering the belly, and all the fat inside the belly.
He shall cut away both its kidneys, the fat at its flanks, and the smaller lobe of its liver along with its kidneys.
The priest shall place it on the altar. It is his offering to the Lord.
If his offering to the Lord is from the goats, he shall bring it before the Lord.
He shall lay his hand on its head, and they shall slaughter it before the Lord at the entrance to the tent of testimony. Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall pour its blood all around the altar.
From it he shall take an offering to the Lord: the fat covering its belly and all the fat inside its belly;
He shall remove both kidneys, all the fat on them that is by the flanks, and the smaller lobe of the liver together with the kidneys.
and the priest shall place it on the altar. It is an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
All fat belongs to the Lord. This is a perpetual law throughout all your generations, wherever you live: you shall eat neither any fat nor any blood.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: If anyone sins [unknowingly] by doing any one of the things that the Lord’s commandments forbid;
if it is the anointed high priest who sins among the people, he shall bring to the Lord, for the sin he has committed, a bull from the herd without blemish as an offering for his sin.
He shall bring that bull to the entrance to the tent of testimony before the Lord. He shall lay his hand on the bull’s head and slaughter the bull before the Lord.
The anointed and ordained priest shall take some of the bull’s blood in his hand and bring it into the tent of testimony.
The priest shall dip his finger into the blood and sprinkle some of that blood with his finger seven times before the Lord, on the curtain of the sanctuary.

The priest shall put some of the bull’s blood on the horns of the incense altar that is set before the Lord in the curtained tabernacle. He shall pour out all its blood at the base of the altar of offering, which is at the entrance to the curtained tabernacle.
He shall strip away all the fat of the bull offered for sin: the fat covering its internal organs and all the fat among its entrails;
He shall remove both kidneys, the fat on them that is by the flanks, and the smaller lobe of its liver together with its kidneys.
just as they remove it from the bull sacrificed for well-being. The priest shall place it on the altar of offerings.
And the hide of that bull and all its flesh, together with its head, its legs, its belly and its dung.
They shall take the whole bull outside the camp to a clean place where they dump the ashes, and burn it with wood and fire. They shall burn it at the place where the ashes are dumped.
If the whole congregation of the Israelites goes astray, and the matter escapes the congregation’s notice, and they do anything forbidden by any of the Lord’s commandments and afterward feel remorse,
and the sin they committed becomes known to them, their congregation shall bring an unblemished bull from the herd for their sin. They shall bring it to the entrance of the tent of testimony.
The elders of that congregation shall lay their hands on the bull’s head before the Lord, and they shall slaughter the bull before the Lord.
The anointed priest shall bring some of that bull’s blood into the tent of testimony.
The priest shall dip his finger into the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the Lord, in front of the sanctuary curtain.

The priest shall put some of its blood on the horns of the altar that stands before the Lord inside the tent of testimony. He shall pour out all its blood at the base of the altar for offerings, which stands at the entrance of the tent of testimony.
He shall strip all the fat from it and put it on the altar.
He shall do with this bull just as they do with the bull for the sin offering. He shall do the same with it. The priest shall make atonement for them, and they will be forgiven.
They shall take that bull outside the camp and burn it just as they burn the first bull, for it is the congregation’s sin offering.
If a ruler sins and unintentionally does anything forbidden by any of the commandments of the Lord their God, and feels remorse,
and the sin he committed becomes known to him, he shall bring as his offering an unblemished male goat from the flock.
He shall lay his hands on the goat’s head, and they shall slaughter it before the Lord in the place where they slaughter the animals for sacrifice, for it is a sin offering.
The priest shall use his finger to put some of the blood of the sin offering on the horns of the altar for offerings. He shall pour out all its blood at the base of the altar for offerings.
He shall place all its fat on the altar, as with the offering of fat from the peace offering. The priest shall make atonement for him, and his sin will be forgiven.
If one person from among the people of the land sins unintentionally, doing anything forbidden by the Lord’s commandments, and feels remorse,
and the sin he committed becomes known to him, he shall bring an unblemished female goat from the flock. He shall bring it for the sin he committed.
He shall lay his hands on the head of the animal he brought for his sin, and they shall slaughter that goat as a sin offering in the place where they slaughter the sacrificial animals.
The priest shall take some of its blood with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar for offerings. He shall pour out all its blood at the base of the altar.

He shall cut off all its fat, just as they cut off the fat of the peace offering. The priest shall place it on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the Lord. The priest shall make atonement for him, and he will be forgiven.
If he brings a sheep as his offering for his sin, he shall bring an unblemished female.
He shall lay his hands on the head of the animal offered for his sin, and they shall slaughter it for his sin in the place where they slaughter the animals for sacrifice.
The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar for offerings. He shall pour out all its blood at the base of the altar.

He shall cut off all its fat, just as they cut off the fat of the sheep offered as a peace offering. The priest shall place it on the altar among the offerings to the Lord. The priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he committed, and he will be forgiven.
If a person sins when he is a witness and hears the words placing him under oath, and he knows about the matter and has seen it, but does not make it known, he will be guilty of sin.
If anyone touches anything unclean, whether a dead thing, something torn by a wild beast that is not clean, an unclean corpse that is not clean, or the carcass of an animal that is not clean;
or if he touches human uncleanness, any uncleanness that makes him unclean when he touches it, even without knowing it, and afterward becomes aware of it and incurs guilt;

or if anyone swears, speaking with his lips to do evil or to do good, concerning anything about which a person may swear without knowing it, and afterward becomes aware of it and is guilty in one of these matters;
he must confess the sin he has committed.

He must bring to the LORD, for the sin he has committed, a ewe from the flock or a female goat from the goats as a sin offering. The priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and his sin will be forgiven.

But if he does not have the means and cannot afford the price of a sheep, he must bring to the LORD two turtledoves or two young pigeons for the sin he has committed, one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering.
He must bring them to the priest, and the priest shall present the one for the sin offering first. The priest shall cut its neck without severing its head.
He shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar, and let the remaining blood drain out at the base of the altar, because it is a sin offering.
He shall offer the second as a burnt offering according to its prescribed rule. The priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven.

But if he does not have the means and cannot afford a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons, he must bring as his offering for his sin a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a sin offering. He must not put oil in it or place frankincense on it, because it is a sin offering.
He must bring it to the priest, and the priest shall take a handful of it as its memorial portion and put it on the altar upon the offering to the LORD, because it is a sin offering.
The priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed in any of these matters, and he will be forgiven. What remains shall belong to the priest, as with the offering of fine flour.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said:

If anyone commits an offense and unintentionally sins concerning the LORD’s holy things, he must bring to the LORD as his guilt offering an unblemished ram from the flock, valued in shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, for the guilt he has incurred.

He must repay what he has wrongfully taken from the holy things, add a fifth to it, and give it to the priest. The priest shall make atonement for him with that ram of his guilt offering, and he will be forgiven.
If anyone sins and unknowingly does anything that the LORD’s commandments forbid, and incurs guilt because of the sin that has come upon him,

he must bring to the priest an unblemished ram from the flock, valued in silver, as his guilt offering. The priest shall make atonement for him for the offense he committed without knowing it, and he will be forgiven.
For he is guilty; he has indeed incurred guilt before the LORD.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said:

If anyone sins, goes astray, and disregards the LORD’s command, and lies to his neighbor about something entrusted to him, about something they held in partnership, or about something he stole, or if he has defrauded his neighbor;
or if he finds something lost and lies about it and swears falsely concerning any of these things that people do and in which they must not sin;
then, when he has sinned and afterward incurs guilt, he must return what he took by theft, what he obtained through oppression and fraud, anything entrusted to his care, or the lost thing he found;
For anything about which he has sworn falsely, he must restore the full value of the property and add a fifth of its value to it. He must return it to its owner on the day he is convicted.
He must bring to the Lord, as his guilt offering, an unblemished ram from the flock, at the valuation for his guilt offering.
The priest must make atonement for him before the Lord, and he will be forgiven for any of the things he has done for which he incurred guilt.

The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him, “Command Aaron and his sons and tell them: This is the law of the burnt offering, and this is its prescribed procedure: Leave the burnt offering on the altar until morning, while the altar fire burns upon it.”
The priest must put on a linen garment and wear linen trousers over his body. He must remove from the altar the ashes of the offering that the fire has consumed and place them beside the altar.
He must take off those garments and put on other garments, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.
The fire must burn on the altar and must not go out. Every morning the priest must burn wood on it, arrange the burnt offering on it, and put the fat of the peace offering on it.
The fire shall burn continually on the altar and shall not go out.
This is the law for the grain offering that Aaron’s sons shall bring to the altar before the Lord.

He shall take a handful of the fine flour of the grain offering, together with its oil and all the frankincense on the offering, and put it on the altar, for it is its memorial offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Aaron and his sons must eat what remains of it. They must eat it unleavened in a holy place; they must eat it in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
They must not leaven it for baking.
This is their portion, which I have given them from the offerings to the Lord. It is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
Every male among the priests may eat it. This is a lasting ordinance throughout your generations concerning the offerings to the Lord. Whoever touches it will become holy.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:

“This is what I have granted to Aaron and his sons from what they bring to the Lord, from the day he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah measure of fine flour as a regular offering, half in the morning and half toward evening.
They must prepare it with oil on a griddle and bring it kneaded, for it is an offering of broken pieces, an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
The priest from among his sons who is anointed in his place must prepare it. This is a lasting ordinance, to be observed at all times.”
Every grain offering of a priest shall be burned completely; none of it shall be eaten.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Tell Aaron and his people: This is the law of the sin offering. In the place where they slaughter the burnt offering, they must also slaughter the sin offering before the Lord. It is most holy.
The priest who offers it shall eat it. They shall eat it in a holy place, within the courtyard of the curtained tabernacle.
Whoever touches that meat will become holy. If any of its blood is splashed on a garment, they must wash the part on which it was splashed in a holy place.
They shall break the earthenware vessel in which it was cooked. If it was cooked in an iron vessel, they shall scour it and wash it with water.
Every male among the priests may eat it. It is most holy and belongs to the Lord.
But no sin offering whose blood is brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the sanctuary may be eaten. They must burn it with fire.
This is the law of the guilt offering. It is most holy.
In the place where they slaughter the burnt offering, they must slaughter the ram for the guilt offering. They must pour its blood all around the base of the altar.
He shall remove all its fat from it, including its fat tail, the fat covering its internal organs, and the fat among its intestines.
He must remove both its kidneys, the fat on them that is on its flanks, and the small lobe of its liver along with its kidneys.
The priest must put it on the altar. It is an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord; it is a guilt offering.
Every male among the priests may eat it. They must eat it in a holy place.
It is most holy.
As with the sin offering, so with the guilt offering: the same law applies to both. It belongs to the priest who makes atonement with them.
The priest who offers a person's sacrifice shall have the hide of the sacrifice that he offered.
Every prepared offering belongs to all the sons of Aaron, to each an equal share.
This is the law of the peace offering that they bring to the Lord.
If he brings it as a thanksgiving offering, he shall bring with the thanksgiving sacrifice bread of fine flour prepared with oil, unleavened wafers spread with oil, and fine flour mixed with oil.
Along with leavened bread, he shall bring his offering for his thanksgiving peace sacrifice.
He shall take one of each kind from his entire offering as a gift to the Lord. It belongs to the priest who sprinkles the blood of that peace offering.
The meat of the peace sacrifice also belongs to him. They shall eat it on the day they bring it, and they shall leave none of it until morning.
But if he brings his offering in fulfillment of a vow or of his own free will, they shall eat it on the day he brings his sacrifice and on the second day.
If any of the meat of his sacrifice remains until the third day, they shall burn it in the fire.

But if they eat any of that meat on the third day, it will not be accepted on behalf of the one who brought it, nor will it be credited to him, because it is unclean. The person who eats any of it shall bear the guilt.
If the meat touches anything unclean, they shall not eat it; they shall burn it in the fire. Anyone who is clean may eat that meat.
Any person who eats meat from the Lord’s sacrifice of well-being while unclean shall be cut off from their people.

If a person touches anything unclean—human uncleanness, an animal that is not clean, or any unclean thing that is not clean—and eats any meat from the Lord's peace sacrifice, that person shall be cut off from their people.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
“Tell the Israelites and say to them: You shall not eat any fat of cattle, sheep, or goats.
The fat of an animal that has died or has been killed by a wild beast may be used for any work, but they must not eat it.
Anyone who eats fat from livestock from which they bring a sacrifice to the Lord shall be cut off from their people.
You shall not eat any blood wherever you live, whether from animals or birds.
Any person who eats blood shall be cut off from their people.”
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: Whoever brings a sacrifice of well-being to the Lord shall bring his offering to the Lord from his sacrifice of well-being.
“With his own hands he shall bring his sacrifice to the Lord. He shall bring the fat of the breast and the small lobe of the liver, so that he may present his offering before the Lord.
The priest shall place the fat of the breast on the altar, but the breast shall belong to Aaron and his sons.
He shall give the right thigh as a contribution to the priest from your sacrifices of well-being.
The one among Aaron's sons who brings the blood and fat of the peace offering shall have the right leg as his share.

For I have taken the breast presented as a contribution and the right thigh from the Israelites, from your sacrifices of well-being, and given them to Aaron the priest and his sons. They shall receive them from the Israelites as a perpetual due.
This is the share of Aaron and his sons from the sacrifices to the Lord, from the day they come to serve as priests to the Lord.
As the Lord commanded, these are to be given to them from among the Israelites, from the day they were anointed. This shall be a perpetual statute for them throughout their generations.
This is the law for offerings and sacrifices, for the sin offering, the guilt offering, the consecration offering, and the peace offering,
as the Lord commanded Moses on Mount Sinai, on the day the Lord commanded the Israelites to bring their offerings before the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said,
“Take Aaron and his sons, their garments, the anointing oil, the bull for the sin offering, two rams, and a basket of unleavened bread.
Gather the whole congregation at the entrance to the tent of testimony.”
Moses did as the Lord commanded him, and he gathered the congregation at the entrance to the tent of testimony.
Moses said to the congregation, “This is what the Lord commanded you to do.”
Moses took Aaron and his sons and washed them with water.
He dressed him in the tunic, fastened the sash around him, clothed him in the robe, and put the ephod on him. He fastened the woven band of the ephod around him and secured it with the band.
He put the breastpiece on him and placed revelation and truth on the breastpiece.
He put the turban on his head and placed the most holy gold plate on the front of the turban, as the Lord commanded Moses.
Moses took some of the anointing oil.

He sprinkled some of it on the altar seven times. He anointed the altar and consecrated it, along with all its utensils, and the basin and its stand, and consecrated them. He anointed the tent and consecrated it and all its furnishings.
Moses poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head, anointed him, and consecrated him.
Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward, dressed them in tunics, fastened sashes around them, and put turbans on them, as the Lord commanded Moses.
He brought forward the bull for the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the bull for the sin offering.

They slaughtered it, and Moses took some of its blood and, with his finger, put it on the horns all around the altar, purifying the altar. He poured the blood at the base of the altar and consecrated it, so that atonement could be made on it.
Moses took the fat on the internal organs, the small lobe of the liver, both kidneys, and the fat on them, and Moses placed them on the altar.
He burned the bull, its hide, its flesh, and its dung with fire outside the camp, as the Lord commanded Moses.
Moses brought forward the ram for the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.
Moses slaughtered the ram, and Moses poured its blood all around the altar.
He cut the ram into its separate pieces, and Moses laid out its head, its pieces, and its fat.
He washed its entrails and its legs with water, and Moses placed the whole ram on the altar. It was a burnt offering with a pleasing aroma, an offering to the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.
Moses brought forward the second ram, the ram of consecration, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.
They slaughtered it, and Moses took some of its blood and put it on Aaron’s right earlobe, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.

Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward, and Moses put some of that blood on their right earlobes, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Moses poured the blood around the altar.
Moses took its fat, its rump, the fat of its belly, the lobe of its liver, both its kidneys and the fat on them, and its right thigh.
From the basket of consecration that was before the Lord, he took one unleavened loaf, one loaf made with oil, and one wafer, and placed them on the fat and on the right thigh.
He placed all of it in Aaron’s hands and in his sons’ hands, and they presented it as an offering before the Lord.
Moses took it from their hands and placed it on the altar, on top of the consecration sacrifice. It was an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Moses took the breast from the ram of consecration and cut it off to present it before the Lord. It became Moses’ share, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood on the altar and sprinkled it on Aaron and his clothes, and on his sons and their clothes with him. He consecrated Aaron and his clothes, and his sons and their clothes with him.

Moses said to Aaron and his sons, “Boil the meat in the courtyard of the tent of testimony, in a holy place, and eat it there, together with the bread in the basket of consecration, as he commanded me, saying, ‘Aaron and his sons shall eat it.’
Burn whatever remains of the meat and the bread in the fire.
Do not go out through the entrance of the tent of testimony for seven days, until you have completed the days of your consecration, for he will consecrate you over seven days.
What was done on this day is what the Lord commanded to be done to make atonement for you.”
You shall remain at the entrance to the curtained tabernacle for seven days, night and day, and keep the Lord’s command so that you do not die, for this is what the Lord commanded me.
Aaron and his sons did everything that the Lord had commanded Moses.
On the eighth day, Moses called Aaron, his sons, and the elders of Israel.
He said to Aaron, “Take for yourself a calf from the herd as a sin offering and a ram as a burnt offering, and bring them before the Lord.
Speak to the elders of Israel and tell them: Take one male goat as a sin offering, and a sheep, a bull, and a year-old calf, without blemish, as an offering.
Also bring a calf from the herd and a ram as a peace offering before the Lord, and fine flour mixed with oil, for today the Lord will appear to you.”
They brought what Moses had commanded before the tent of testimony, and the whole congregation came and stood before the Lord.
Moses said to them, “This is what the Lord told you to do. Do it, and the glory of the Lord will appear to you.”

Moses said to Aaron, “Go to the altar and offer your sin offering and your burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and your household. Then offer the people's sacrifice and make atonement for them, as the Lord commanded.”
Aaron went to the altar and slaughtered the calf as an offering for his sin.
Aaron’s sons brought its blood to him. He dipped his finger in the blood and put it on the horns of the altar, and he poured its blood at the base of the altar.
He placed the fat, both kidneys, and the lobe of the liver from the sin offering on the altar, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
But they burned its flesh and its hide with fire outside the camp.
He also slaughtered the burnt offering. Aaron’s sons brought its blood to him, and he poured it around the altar.
They brought him the burnt offering piece by piece, together with its head, and he placed it on the altar.
He washed its entrails and its legs and placed them on the altar, on top of the burnt offering.
Then he brought the people's offering. He took the goat for the people's sin offering, slaughtered it, purified it, and cut it up as he had the first one.
He brought the burnt offering and offered it according to the prescribed rule.
He brought the grain offering, filled his hands with some of it, and put it on the altar, in addition to the morning offering.
Then he slaughtered the ox and the ram as the people's peace offering. Aaron's sons brought him the blood, and he poured it around the altar.
And the fat of both the ox and the sheep, its fat tail, the fat covering its belly, its two kidneys and the fat on them, and the small lobe of its liver.
He placed the fat on the breast and put it on the altar.
He set apart the breast and the right thigh for Aaron as his gift before the Lord, as he had commanded Moses.
Aaron raised his hands over the people and blessed them. Then he came down, having performed the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offering.
Moses and Aaron entered the tent of testimony. When they came out, they blessed all the people, and the glory of the Lord appeared to all the people.
Fire came out from the Lord and consumed the offering on the altar, along with the fat. All the people saw it, were awestruck, and fell on their faces.
Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu each took his incense burner, put fire in them, and added incense. They brought before the Lord fire from another source, which the Lord had not commanded them to bring.
Fire came out from the Lord and consumed them, and they died before the Lord.
Moses said to Aaron, “This is what the Lord said: ‘Among those who approach me I will be shown to be holy, and before the whole congregation I will be glorified.’” And Aaron was stunned.
Moses summoned Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel, Aaron's paternal uncle, and said to them, “Go, take your brothers away from the sanctuary and carry them outside the camp.”
They went in and carried them outside the camp in their tunics, as Moses had told them.

Moses said to Aaron and his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, “Do not shave your heads or tear your clothes, so that you do not die and wrath does not come upon the whole congregation. But let your brothers, the whole house of Israel, mourn those who were burned, whom the Lord burned.
Do not go out through the entrance of the tent of testimony, so that you do not die, for the Lord's anointing oil is upon you.” They did as Moses told them.
The Lord spoke to Aaron and said:
“You and your sons with you must not drink wine or mead when you enter the tent of testimony or approach the altar, so that you do not die. This is a lasting law throughout your generations,
by which a distinction is made between holy and unholy things, and between clean things and things that are not clean.”
And you shall teach the Israelites all the laws that the Lord told them through Moses.
Moses said to Aaron and his surviving sons Eleazar and Ithamar, “Take the grain offering left over from the Lord's offering and eat it unleavened beside the altar. It is most holy.
For it is your allotted portion and your sons' allotted portion from the Lord's offerings, because this is what the Lord commanded me.

You, your sons, and your household with you shall eat the breast of the contribution and the thigh of the contribution in a holy place. They are your allotted portion and your sons' allotted portion, given to you from the peace offerings of the Israelites.

They shall bring the thigh of the contribution and the breast that is set apart, together with the offering of fat, having separated them out, and shall set them apart before the Lord. They shall belong to you and your sons with you as a lasting entitlement, as the Lord commanded Moses.”
Moses searched for the goat of the sin offering, and when he searched, it had been completely burned up. Moses became angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's surviving sons.

He said to them, “Why did you not eat the sin offering in a holy place? It is most holy, and he gave it to you to eat so that you might remove the congregation's sin and make atonement for them before the Lord.
Since its blood was not brought inside the sanctuary before him, you were to eat it in a holy place, as I was commanded.”

Aaron spoke to Moses and said to him, “Today, when they offered their sin offering and their sacrifice before the Lord, this happened to me. So now it would not be good before the Lord for me to eat the sin offering.”
Moses heard this and approved.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
Tell the Israelites and say to them, “These are the animals you may eat from among all the animals on the earth.
You may eat any animal that has a divided hoof, with its hoof split down the middle into two parts, and that chews the cud.
But these you must not eat from among those that chew the cud or have divided hooves: the camel, because it chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof. It is unclean for you.
And the hare, because it chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof. It too is unclean for you.
And the hyrax, because it chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof. It too is unclean for you.
And the pig, because it has a divided hoof, split down the middle, but does not chew the cud. It too is unclean for you.
You must not eat their meat or touch their carcasses, because they are unclean for you.
These you may eat from among everything in the water: anything that has fins and scales and lives in the water, in the seas or in the rivers. These you may eat.
But anything in the water, in the seas or in the rivers, that has no fins and scales—from everything the water brings forth and every living creature in the water—is unclean.
They shall be unclean for you. You must not eat their meat, and you must regard their carcasses as detestable.
Anything in the water that has no fins and scales is unclean for you.
These are the birds you must regard as detestable and must not eat, because they are unclean: the eagle, the griffon vulture, and the osprey;
the vulture, the owl, and the kite and all others of its kind;
the raven and all others of its kind;
the ostrich and all others of its kind, the gull and others of its kind, and the hawk and others of its kind;
the night owl, the cormorant, and the ibis;
the swamphen, the pelican, and the swan;
the heron, the plover and others of its kind, the hoopoe, and the bat.
Every swarming winged creature that walks on four legs is unclean for you.
But these you may eat from among the swarming winged creatures that walk on four legs: those that have jointed legs above their feet with which to spring above the ground.

These are the ones you may eat: the dagebya [?] and others of its kind, the attacus locust and others of its kind, the snake-fighting locust and others of its kind, and the locust and others of its kind.
Any flying creature that has four feet is unclean for you.
Through these you become unclean.
Anyone who touches their carcasses is unclean until evening.
Anyone who picks up their carcasses must wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening.
Every animal whose hoof is divided and whose claws are separated, but which does not chew the cud, is unclean for you. Anyone who touches their carcasses is unclean.
Among all the beasts that walk on four legs, everything that walks on its paws is unclean for you. Anyone who touches their carcasses will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who carries their carcasses must wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening. These are unclean for you.
Among the living creatures that move about on the ground, these are unclean for you: the mouse, [?], [?], [?], [?], [?], the weasel, the chameleon, and the mole.
These are unclean for you among all the living creatures that move on the earth. Anyone who touches their carcasses will be unclean until evening.

Anything into which their carcasses fall is unclean, whether a wooden article, clothing, a skin, or a sack—any article used for work. It must be immersed in water and will be unclean until evening; afterward it will be clean.
Any earthenware vessel into whose hollow any of these falls is unclean, since it has fallen inside it. You must break it.
Any vessel from which you eat food, if water has been put into it, is unclean for you. A drinking vessel from which you drink is also unclean.
Anything into which their carcasses fall is unclean. If it is an oven or a stand for cooking pots, you must demolish it, because it is unclean and is unclean for you.
But springs of water, cisterns, and pools of water are clean for you. Anyone who touches their carcasses is unclean.
If their carcasses fall on any seed intended for sowing, it is clean.
But if water has been poured on any seed and their carcass falls on it, it is unclean for you.
If an animal that you may eat dies, anyone who touches its carcass will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who eats its dead body shall wash his clothes and is unclean until evening. Anyone who picks up their carcass shall wash his clothes and is unclean until evening.
Every creature that crawls on the earth is unclean for you, and you must not eat it.

Everything that moves on its belly, everything that always walks on four legs, and everything with many legs, among all the creatures that crawl on the earth—you must not eat them, because they are unclean for you.
Do not defile yourselves with any of the creatures that crawl on the earth. Do not become defiled by them or become unclean through them.
For I am the Lord your God. Sanctify yourselves and be holy, because I am the Lord your God; I am holy. Do not make yourselves abominable through any of the creatures that crawl on the earth.
For I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. You must be holy, because I am holy.
This is the law concerning animals, birds, every living creature that moves in the water, and every living creature that moves on the earth:
It distinguishes between the unclean and the clean. You must instruct the Israelites concerning the living creatures they may eat and the living creatures they may not eat.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: If a woman conceives and gives birth to a male child, she will be unclean for seven days. She will be unclean as she is during the days of her menstrual period.
On the eighth day she must circumcise the foreskin of his member.
She shall remain for thirty-three days in purification from her bleeding. She shall not touch anything holy or enter the sanctuary until the days of her purification are completed.
But if she gives birth to a girl, she is unclean for two weeks, as during her menstrual period, and she shall remain for sixty-six days in purification from her bleeding.

When the days of her purification are completed, whether for a son or a daughter, she must bring a year-old lamb as a sacrifice and a young pigeon or a turtledove as a sin offering to the priest at the entrance of the tent of testimony.
He must bring it before the Lord, and the priest must make atonement for her and purify her from her flow of blood. This is the law for a woman who gives birth, whether to a male or a female child.

But if she does not have the means and cannot afford a sheep, she shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and one for a sin offering. The priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be clean.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
If an ash-like mark appears on the surface of a person's skin and turns white, becoming a leprous discoloration in his skin, he must go to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons who are priests.

The priest shall examine the spot on the skin. If the hair in the spot has changed and turned white, and the spot appears deeper than the surrounding skin, it is a spot of leprosy. The priest shall examine it and declare the person unclean.

But if it is a white spot on the skin, and it does not appear deeper than the skin, and its hair has not changed or turned white, and the spot itself is not clearly visible, the priest shall isolate the person for seven days because of that spot.
On the seventh day the priest shall examine the spot. If he finds that it remains unchanged before him and has not spread on the skin, the priest shall isolate the person for another seven days.

The priest shall examine him again on the seventh day. If the spot is not clearly visible and has not spread on the skin, the priest shall declare him clean, because it is only a mark. He shall wash his clothes and be clean.
But if that spot changes and becomes worse in his skin after the priest has examined him and pronounced him clean, he shall go to the priest again.
The priest shall examine him. If the spot has worsened on the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean, because it is leprosy.
If a spot of leprosy breaks out on a person, he shall go to the priest.
The priest shall examine him. If there is something like a white swelling on his skin, and it has produced white hair, with raw flesh in it, in the healthy, living skin,
that is a white mark, and the priest shall declare him unclean. He shall not isolate him, because he is unclean.
But if leprosy breaks out on his skin, and the spots of leprosy cover all his skin, from his head to his feet, everywhere the priest can see,
and the priest sees that the leprosy has covered the entire surface of his skin, he shall declare him clean, because his whole body has changed and turned white. For this reason he is clean.
But on the day when a patch of healthy flesh appears on him, he shall be unclean.
The priest shall examine that patch of healthy flesh and declare him unclean. That patch of healthy flesh makes him unclean, because it has become leprosy.
But if that patch of healthy flesh disappears, changes, and turns white, he shall go to the priest.
The priest shall examine him. If the spot has changed and turned white, the priest shall declare the spot clean, because the person has become clean.
If his flesh breaks out in a swollen sore and his wound heals,
and in the place of his wound something white appears, like a swelling that looks very white or reddish, he shall show it to the priest.
If it is deeper than his skin, and its hair has changed and turned white, the priest shall declare him unclean, because it is a spot of leprosy that has broken out in the swelling.
But if the priest examines him and there is no white hair in it, and it is not deeper than the surface of his skin, and the spot itself is not visible, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.
If it spreads on his skin, the priest shall declare him unclean, because it is a spot of leprosy that has broken out in the swelling.
But if the spot remains in its place and has not spread, it is the swelling of the wound, and the priest shall declare him clean.
If the flesh of his skin breaks open from a burn caused by fire, and a white spot, reddish or very white, appears in the skin that has healed from the burn,

the priest shall examine it. If it has produced white hair that is visible, and it appears deeper than his skin, it is leprosy that has broken out in the burn. The priest shall declare him unclean, because it is a spot of leprosy.
But if the priest examines him and there is no visible white hair in it, and it is not deeper than his skin, and the spot itself is not visible, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.
The priest shall examine him on the seventh day. If it has spread in his skin, the priest shall pronounce him unclean, because it is a leprous spot and has broken out in [?].

But if the spot remains in its place and has not spread on the skin, and the spot itself is not visible, it is the swelling of the burn. The priest shall declare him clean, because it is the site of the burn.
If a man or woman develops a discolored patch of leprosy on the head or in the beard,

the priest shall examine the patch. If it looks worse than the surrounding skin and fine white hair has grown in it, the priest shall declare the person unclean, because it is a sign of leprosy of the head or leprosy of the beard.

But if the priest examines the discoloration of this mark and it does not look worse than the surrounding skin, and there is no white hair in it, the priest shall isolate the person with this discolored mark for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest shall examine the patch. If the patch has not spread, there is no white hair in it, and it does not look worse than the surrounding skin,
when the person shaves that area of the skin, the discolored patch must not be removed [?]. The priest shall isolate the person with the patch for another seven days.

On the seventh day the priest shall examine the patch. If the patch has not spread on the skin after the person shaved, and the patch does not look worse than the surrounding skin, the priest shall declare the person clean. After washing their clothes, the person will be clean.
But if the patch spreads on the skin after the person has been declared clean,
the priest shall examine the person. If the patch has spread on the skin, the priest shall not look for white hair, because the person is unclean.
But if the patch remains in its place and black hair grows in it, the patch has healed. The person is clean, and the priest shall declare the person clean.
If a man or a woman has an eruption in the skin of the body, bright or whitish;
The priest shall examine it. If it is bright or whitish on the skin of the person's body, it is a mottled patch that has appeared on the skin of the body, and the person is clean.
If someone's head has lost its hair, that person is bald and is clean.
But if his head has lost its hair toward the front, he is bald at the forehead and is clean.
But if a white or reddish spot appears on his bald crown or his bald forehead, it is leprosy that has broken out on his bald crown or his bald forehead.
The priest shall examine it, and if the appearance of the spot on his bald crown or his bald forehead is white or reddish, like the appearance of leprosy in the skin of his body;
The man has leprosy, and the priest shall immediately examine the patch on his head or on his forehead.
The person with leprosy, on whom this discolored patch of leprosy is present, shall keep their clothes unfastened and their head uncovered. They shall cover their mouth and be called unclean.
For as long as the leprosy remains on the person, they are unclean and shall remain unclean. They shall live apart, and their dwelling shall be outside the camp.
If a sign of leprosy appears in clothing, whether in woolen clothing or linen clothing,
whether in the warp or the weft, whether in linen or wool, whether in leather or in anything made of leather,
and a greenish or reddish patch appears in the leather or clothing, whether in its warp or its weft, or in any leather article, it is a patch of leprosy and shall be shown to the priest.
The priest shall examine that spot, and the priest shall keep that spot under observation for seven days.

The priest shall examine the patch on the seventh day. If the patch has spread in the clothing, whether in its warp or its weft, or in the leather or anything made of leather, it is leprosy that does not go away.

They shall burn the clothing, whether the patch is in its warp or its weft, whether it is wool or linen, or in any leather article in which the patch has appeared. Because it is leprosy that does not go away, they shall burn it with fire.
But if the priest examines it and the patch has not spread in the clothing, whether in its warp or its weft, or in the leather article,
the priest shall order them to wash the place where the patch appeared, and the priest shall isolate the affected article for another seven days.

The priest shall examine the spot after it has been washed. If it has not changed its appearance, even if the spot has not spread, the article is unclean. They shall burn it in fire, because the spot has taken hold in the garment, its warp, or its weft.
But if the priest examines it and the spot is no longer visible after washing, they shall tear out the affected part from the garment, the warp, the weft, or the leather.
If it appears again in the garment, the warp, the weft, or any leather article, it is leprosy. They shall burn in fire the article in which the spot has appeared.
But if the garment, the warp, the weft, or any leather article has been washed and the spot has disappeared from it, they shall wash it a second time, and it shall be clean.
This is the law concerning a leprous spot that appears in a garment, whether woolen or linen, in the warp or the weft, or in any leather article, for declaring it clean or unclean.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
This is the law for a person with leprosy on the day of his cleansing: he shall go to the priest.
The priest shall go outside the camp and examine the person. If the leprous spot has left the person with leprosy,
then, when the priest has gone to him, the person who has become clean shall bring two live, clean birds, cedarwood, twisted scarlet thread, and hyssop leaves.
The priest shall give the order, and they shall slaughter one bird in fresh water in an earthenware vessel.
He shall bring cedarwood, and the priest shall take the live bird and release it into the open country after dipping it in the blood of the bird that was slaughtered.

Then he shall dip the cedarwood, the twisted scarlet thread, and the hyssop leaves in the blood of the bird slaughtered in fresh water. He shall sprinkle the person being cleansed of leprosy seven times, and that person shall be clean.

The person being cleansed shall wash his clothes, shave off all his hair, and bathe in water, and he shall be clean. After that he may enter the camp, but he shall remain outside his house for seven days.
On the seventh day he shall shave all the hair of his head, his beard, and his eyebrows; he shall shave off all his hair. He shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and he shall be clean.
On the eighth day he shall bring two unblemished lambs a year old, and also one more unblemished lamb a year old, three measures of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and one cup of oil.
The priest who cleanses him shall present the man being cleansed, together with these things, before the Lord at the entrance to the tent of testimony.
The priest shall take one sheep and bring it as a guilt offering, together with that measure of oil, and shall set them apart as an offering before the Lord.
They shall slaughter the lamb in the holy place where they slaughter the burnt offering and the sin offering. For the sin offering, like the guilt offering, belongs to the priest; it is most holy.
The priest shall take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the right ear of the person being cleansed, on his thumb, and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest shall take some of the oil from the cup and pour it into his left hand.
The priest shall dip his right finger into the oil in his left hand and sprinkle some of the oil seven times before the Lord.

The priest shall put some of the oil remaining in his hand on the tip of the right ear of the person being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, where the blood of the guilt offering was placed.
The priest shall put the oil remaining in his hand on the head of the person being cleansed, and the priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord.
The priest shall offer the sin offering and make atonement for the person being cleansed because of his sin. After that the priest shall slaughter the burnt offering.
The priest shall bring the sacrifice and the offering onto the altar before the Lord. The priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be clean.

But if he is poor and does not have the means, he shall bring one male lamb to be set apart as a guilt offering, with which atonement is to be made for him, one measure of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and one cupful of oil;
and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, whichever he can afford. One shall be for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering.
He shall bring them on the eighth day for his cleansing, taking them to the priest at the entrance to the tent of testimony, before the Lord.
The priest shall take the lamb for the guilt offering and the cupful of oil and present them as an offering before the Lord.

He shall slaughter the lamb for the guilt offering. The priest shall take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the right earlobe of the person being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest shall pour some of that oil into his left hand.
With his right finger, the priest shall sprinkle some of the oil in his left hand seven times before the Lord.

From the oil remaining in his hand, the priest shall put some on the right earlobe of the person being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, where the blood of the guilt offering was put.
The priest shall put the rest of the oil remaining in his hand on the head of the person being cleansed. The priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord.
He shall offer one of those turtledoves or young pigeons, whichever he can afford;
one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, together with the grain offering. The priest shall make atonement before the Lord for the person being cleansed.
This is the law for someone on whom a mark of leprosy has appeared and who does not have the means for his cleansing.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
When you enter the land of Canaan, which I am giving you to possess, and I send a sign of leprosy into the houses of the land you possess,
the person in whose house it appears shall tell the priest, saying, “I have seen something like a sign of leprosy in my house.”

The priest shall order the belongings to be removed from that house before he enters to inspect the sign of leprosy, so that everything in the house will not become unclean. Afterward the priest shall enter to inspect the house.
The priest shall examine the sign of leprosy. If the sign of leprosy on the walls of the house is greenish or reddish and appears sunken below the surface of the walls,
the priest shall go out of the house through the doorway and close up the house for seven days.
The priest shall return on the seventh day and inspect the house. If the discoloration has spread on the walls of the house,
The priest shall give orders, and they shall remove the stones where the sign of leprosy is found and take them outside the town to an unclean place.
they shall bring other cut stones and put them in place of those stones. They shall bring other earth and plaster the house.
But if the discoloration returns and appears in the house after they have removed its stones, scraped the house, and plastered it,
the priest shall enter and inspect it. If the discoloration has spread in the house, it is persistent leprosy in the house; it is unclean.
They shall demolish the house and dump its timbers, its stones, and all the earth from the house outside the town in an unclean place.
Anyone who enters that house during any of the days since it was shut up is unclean until evening.
Anyone who sleeps in that house must wash his clothes, and anyone who eats in it must wash his clothes.

But if the priest comes and enters and sees that the discoloration has not spread in the house after it was plastered, the priest shall declare the house clean, because the discoloration has gone away.
To purify the house, he shall take two birds, cedarwood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop leaves.
He shall slaughter one of the birds in an earthenware vessel over fresh water.

He shall take the cedarwood, the scarlet yarn, the hyssop leaves, and the living bird, and dip them in the blood of the bird slaughtered over fresh water. With them he shall sprinkle the house seven times.
He shall purify the house with the bird's blood, the fresh water, the living bird, the cedarwood, the hyssop leaves, and the scarlet yarn.
He shall send the living bird outside the town and release it in the open country. He shall make atonement for the house, and the house shall be clean.
This is the law for every sign of leprosy and its discoloration;
for leprosy in clothing and in a house;
and for signs of swelling and spots;
so that you may know whether it is unclean or clean. This is the law for leprosy.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: Any man who has a discharge is unclean.

This is the law concerning the uncleanness of a man whose semen flows from his body and whose discharge remains in his body: this is the uncleanness upon him. Throughout all the days when the discharge continues to flow from his body, that discharge makes him unclean.
Every bed on which he lies is unclean, [and every object on which he sits becomes unclean.
] Anyone who touches his bed must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and he is unclean until evening.
Anyone who sits on an object on which that man sat must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he is unclean until evening.
[Anyone who touches the man whose semen is discharging must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and he is unclean until evening.
] If he spits on someone who is clean, that person must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he is unclean until evening.
Every saddle on which he sits is unclean.
Anyone who touches anything on which he sat is unclean until evening. Anyone who sees him must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and he is unclean until evening.
Anyone whom the man whose semen is discharging touches without washing his hands must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and he is unclean until evening.
Every earthenware vessel that he touches must be broken. A wooden vessel must be washed with water, and it shall be clean.
But if his discharge ceases, seven days shall be counted for his purification. He must wash his clothes and bathe his body in fresh water, and he shall be clean.
On the eighth day he shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them before the Lord, to the entrance of the tent of testimony, and give them to the priest.
The priest shall offer one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord because of his discharge.
If a man has slept with a woman, he shall wash his whole body with water, and he is unclean until evening.
Every garment and every piece of leather that semen has touched shall be washed with water, and it is unclean until evening.
If a woman has slept with a man, they shall wash with water, and they are unclean until evening.
If a woman has a discharge of blood, and it continues to flow from her body, her menstrual period shall last seven days. Anyone who touches her is unclean until evening.
Everything on which she lies while she is menstruating is unclean, and everything on which she sits becomes unclean.
Anyone who touches her bed shall wash his clothes and wash his body, and he is unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches any object on which she has sat shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.
And if she is on her bed or on an object on which she sits, whoever touches it shall be unclean until evening.
If a man lies with her, her uncleanness shall come upon him, and he shall be unclean for seven days. Every bed on which he lies shall be unclean.

If a woman has a discharge of blood for many days, longer than the days of her menstrual period, or if she has a discharge after her menstrual period, she is unclean throughout all the days of her discharge, just as she is unclean during her menstrual period.

Every bed on which she lies throughout the days of her discharge is to her like the bed of her menstrual period. Every object on which she sits is unclean, just as it is unclean during her menstrual period.
Anyone who touches her is unclean. He shall wash his clothes and wash with water, and he is unclean until evening.
But if her discharge stops, seven days shall be counted for her, and afterward she shall be clean.
On the eighth day she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest, to the entrance of the tent of testimony.
The priest shall offer one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for her before the Lord for her unclean discharge.
Keep the Israelites clean from their uncleanness, so that they do not die because of their uncleanness and do not defile my tent, which is among them.
This is the law for a man who has a discharge of semen, and for anyone who has slept with a woman and become unclean through her;

and for a woman who has a discharge of blood during her menstrual period, and for anyone whose semen flows during the days of discharge, whether male or female, and for a man who has slept with a menstruating woman.
The Lord spoke to Moses after the death of Aaron’s two sons, who brought foreign fire before the Lord and died.

The Lord said to Moses, “Tell your brother Aaron not to enter the holy place at any time, inside the curtain, before the mercy seat above the ark, so that he does not die, for I have appeared only in a cloud.”
Then Aaron shall enter the holy place with a bull from the herd as a sin offering and a ram as a burnt offering.

He shall put on a holy linen tunic and wear linen undergarments against his body. He shall fasten a linen sash around himself and put on a linen turban, for these are holy garments. After washing his whole body with water, he shall put them on.
From the congregation of the Israelites he shall take two male goats as a sin offering and one ram as a burnt offering.
Aaron shall bring forward the bull for his sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household.
Then he shall make atonement with those two male goats and stand them before the Lord at the entrance of the tent of testimony.
Aaron shall place lots on the two male goats to determine their allotment: one lot for the Lord and one lot for [?].
Aaron shall bring forward the male goat on which the Lord’s lot fell and offer it as a sin offering.
But the goat on which the lot that he brought fell shall be placed alive before the Lord, to make atonement with it and to send it away where they will release it and leave it in the wilderness.
Aaron shall bring forward the bull for his sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household. He shall slaughter that bull for his sin offering.
He shall take a censer and fill it with burning coals from the altar before the Lord. He shall fill his hands with finely ground fragrant incense and bring it inside the curtain.
He shall put the incense in [the censer] before the Lord, and its smoke shall cover the mercy seat that is above the ark, so that he does not die.
He shall take some of the bull's blood and sprinkle it on the mercy seat toward the east. On the face of the mercy seat he shall sprinkle some of that blood seven times with his finger.

He shall slaughter the goat for the people's sin offering before the Lord and bring some of its blood inside the curtain. He shall do with its blood as he did with the bull's blood, sprinkling some of its blood on the mercy seat and in front of the mercy seat.

He shall make atonement for the holy place because of the uncleanness of the Israelites, their transgressions, and all their sins. He shall do the same for the tent of testimony, which was set up among them in the midst of their uncleanness.

No person at all shall be there when he enters the sanctuary to make atonement, and no one shall remain there until he comes out. He shall make atonement for himself, his household, and the whole congregation of Israel.

He shall go out to the altar that stands before the Lord and make atonement for it. He shall take some of the bull's blood and some of the goat's blood and put it on the horns of the altar all around.
He shall sprinkle some of that blood on it with his finger seven times, cleansing it and making it holy from all the uncleanness of the Israelites.
He shall finish making atonement for the holy place, the tent of testimony, and the altar, and shall perform purification for the priests as well. Then he shall bring forward the living goat.

Aaron shall place both his hands on the head of the living goat and confess over it all the sins of the Israelites, all their transgressions, and all their offenses. He shall place (his hands) on the head of the living goat and send it into the wilderness with a man appointed for the task.
That goat shall carry their sins on its head, and the man shall leave the goat in a desolate land where there are no trees.
Aaron shall enter the tent of testimony and take off the linen garments he is wearing, which he put on when entering the sanctuary, and leave them there.

He shall wash his body with water in a holy place and put on his garments. Then he shall go out and offer his sacrifice and the people's sacrifice, and make atonement for himself, his household, and the people, as he does for the priests.
He shall put the fat of the sin offering on the altar.
The one who brought out the goat that they set apart for release shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. After that he may enter the camp.

The bull of the sin offering and the goat of the sin offering, whose blood was brought into the sanctuary to make atonement with it, shall be taken outside the camp. Their hides, their flesh, and their dung shall be burned with fire.
The one who burned them shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. After that he may enter the camp.
This shall be a permanent law for you: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you shall humble yourselves and do no work, whether native-born, a foreigner, or anyone living among you.
For on that day he shall make atonement for you, to cleanse you from all your sins before the Lord, and you shall be clean.
For it is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you shall humble yourselves. It is a permanent law for you.
The priest whom they anointed and whose hands they consecrated to serve as priest after his father shall make atonement. He shall wear the linen clothes, the holy clothes.
He shall make atonement for the Holy of Holies. He shall make atonement for the tent of testimony and the altar, and he shall make atonement for the priests and the whole congregation.
This shall be a permanent law for you, to make atonement for the Israelites for all their sins. He shall do it once a year, as the Lord commanded Moses.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites, and tell them this command that the Lord has given.
And he said: If anyone slaughters a bull, a sheep, or a goat inside the camp or outside the camp,

[And does not bring it] to the entrance of the tent to make it a sacrifice or a choice peace offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord—after slaughtering it elsewhere, he does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of testimony to present an offering to the Lord before the Lord’s tent—that man will be guilty of taking a life. He has shed blood, and that person shall be cut off from his people.

This is so that the Israelites may bring all their sacrifices that they offer in the open country and present them to the Lord at the entrance of the tent of testimony, to the priest, and offer them as peace offerings to the Lord.
The priest shall pour its blood onto the altar before the Lord, at the entrance of the tent of testimony, and offer the fat as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
They shall not offer their sacrifices to worthless idols, after which they prostitute themselves. This shall be a permanent law for you throughout your generations.
Tell them: Any man among the Israelites or among the foreigners living with you who makes a sacrifice or an offering,
and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of testimony to offer it to the Lord—that person shall be cut off from his people.
If anyone among the Israelites or among the foreigners living with you eats any blood, I will set my face against that person who eats blood and destroy that person from among their people.
For the blood is the life of all flesh, and I have appointed it for you as a sacrifice by which you may make atonement for your lives, because a life is redeemed by its blood.
For this reason I said to you Israelites: No person among you shall eat blood, and no foreigner living with you shall eat blood.
Any man among the Israelites or among the foreigners living with you who goes hunting and kills an animal or a bird that you may eat shall pour out its blood and cover it with earth.
For the blood of all flesh is its life. I told the Israelites, ‘You shall not eat the blood of any flesh, because the blood of all flesh is its life, and everyone who eats it shall be cut off.’
Anyone who eats an animal that died on its own or was eaten by a wild animal, whether native-born or a foreigner, shall wash their clothes and bathe in water and shall be unclean until evening.
But if they do not wash their clothes and do not bathe their body in water, the guilt of sin shall be on their own head.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Tell the Israelites and say to them: I am the Lord your God.
Do not follow the practices of the land of Egypt, where you lived, and do not follow the practices of the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you. Do not live according to their laws.
Carry out my judgments, keep my commandments, and live by them. I am the Lord your God.
Keep my commandments and all my judgments, and carry them out, because anyone who carries them out will live by them. I am the Lord your God.
No one shall approach any relative of his own flesh to uncover their nakedness, for I am the Lord.
You shall not uncover your father’s nakedness or your mother’s nakedness. She is your mother; you shall not uncover her nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife, for it is your father’s nakedness.

Do not uncover the nakedness of your sister, whether she is your father's daughter or your mother's daughter. Even if she was born to him outside, and even if she is one of your relatives, do not uncover her nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your son’s daughter or your daughter’s daughter, for their nakedness is your own nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife’s daughter, for she is your sister, your mother’s daughter. You shall not uncover her nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s sister, for she belongs to your father’s family.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister, for she belongs to your mother’s family.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of the wife of your father’s brother, for she is your relative.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your son’s wife.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your brother’s wife; it is your sister’s nakedness.

Do not uncover the nakedness of a woman together with her daughter. Do not take her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter to uncover their nakedness, for they belong to your household, and it is a sin.
You shall not marry a woman together with her sister, making them jealous of one another and uncovering the nakedness of both the one and the other while the first is still alive.
Do not approach a menstruating woman before she is purified to uncover her nakedness while she is still unclean.
Do not approach your neighbor’s wife to lie with her, and do not sow your seed upon her.
Do not bind your children to an angel [?], so that you do not defile the name of the Holy One, for I am the Lord.
Do not lie with a male as with women, for it is unclean.
Do not approach an animal or lie with it to discharge your seed upon it and defile yourself with it. Neither shall a woman approach an animal for it to lie with her, for it is unclean.
Do not make yourselves unclean by any of these things, for by all these things the nations whom I am driving out before you became unclean.
They made the land guilty, and because of this I punished them, and the land vomited out those who lived on it.
Keep all my laws and judgments, and do not do any of these unclean things, neither the native-born nor the foreigner living among you.
For the people who were born in the land before you did all these unclean things and defiled the land.
Do this so that the land does not vomit you out if you defile it, as it vomited out the nations that were before you.
For anyone who does any of these unclean things—that person who does it shall be cut off from their people.
Keep my commandments, so that you do not follow any of the customs of the unclean people who were before you, and do not defile yourselves by them, for I am the Lord your God.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Tell the whole congregation of the children of Israel: Be holy, for I, the Lord your God, am holy.
Each of you shall revere his father and mother, and keep my Sabbaths.
Do not follow other gods, and do not make cast-metal gods for yourselves, for I am the Lord your God.
If you offer a sacrifice of well-being to the Lord, offer it after purifying yourselves.
They shall eat it on the day you sacrifice it and on the following day. If anything remains on the third day, they shall burn it with fire.
But if they eat it, it shall be counted as rejected and shall not be accepted.
Whoever eats it shall incur sin, because he has defiled the Lord’s holy things. The person who ate it shall be cut off from their people.
At harvest time, when you reap your land, do not harvest your fields completely, and do not gather the grain that falls while you are reaping.
Do not strip your vineyard bare when gathering its grapes, and do not gather the fallen grapes of your vineyard. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner, for I am the Lord your God.
Do not steal, do not lie, and let no one deceive another.
Do not swear falsely by my name, and do not profane the holy name of your God, for I am the Lord your God.
Do not oppress your neighbor or rob him, and do not keep your hired worker’s wages with you overnight until morning.
Do not speak evil against a deaf person or put a stumbling block before a blind person. Fear the Lord your God, for I am the Lord your God.
Do not act unjustly in judgment. Do not show favoritism to the poor or favor the powerful. Judge your neighbor justly.
Do not go about deceitfully among your people, and do not stand against your neighbor’s life, for I am the Lord your God.
Do not hate your neighbor in your heart. Rebuke your neighbor and make known to him what is better for him, and do not commit sin because of him.
Do not take revenge for yourself or bear a grudge against the children of your people. Love your neighbor as yourself. I am the Lord your God.
Keep my law. Do not plow with your ox under a different yoke, and do not plant in your vineyard each one's own [?]. Do not wear a garment whose warp and weft are made of two different kinds.

If someone sleeps with a slave woman pledged to a man, whose ransom has not been paid and who has not been set free, the punishment to be imposed on them shall be determined. They shall not be put to death, because she has not been set free.
He shall bring his guilt offering to the Lord at the entrance of the tent of testimony—a ram as a guilt offering.
The priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord with that ram of the guilt offering, because he has repented of the wrong he committed. The sin he committed shall be forgiven him.

When you enter the land that the Lord your God gives you and plant any kind of tree whose fruit is eaten, you shall cleanse it of all its uncleanness. Its fruit for three years shall be unclean for you; do not eat it.
In the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy and offered in praise to the Lord.
In the fifth year eat its fruit. Its produce is yours, for I am the Lord your God.
Do not eat in the mountains. Do not defile yourselves, and do not seek omens from birds.
Do not make tufts from the hair of your heads, and do not shave the beards of your faces.
When someone has died, do not bring a razor against your flesh, and do not make marks on yourselves, for I am the Lord your God.
