Do not defile your daughter or make her a prostitute. Do not let the land practice prostitution and become filled with injustice.
Keep my Sabbath and revere my holy places, for I am the Lord.
Do not follow mediums, and do not follow sorcerers, so that you do not become defiled through them, for I am the Lord your God.
Rise before someone who is gray-haired, honor an elderly person, and fear the Lord your God, for I am the Lord your God.
If a foreigner comes to you, do not mistreat him in your land.
The foreigner who comes to you shall be treated like someone native-born. Love him as yourself, because you were foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
Do not act unjustly in judgment, in counting and calculation, in measuring, or in weighing.
Your scales shall be honest, your measure shall be honest, and your measure of capacity shall be honest, for I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
Keep all my laws and all my commandments, and carry them out, for I am the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:

Tell the Israelites: If anyone among the Israelites or among the foreigners who have come into Israel dedicates his offspring to an angel, he shall surely be put to death. The people of the land shall stone him.
I will set my face against that man and destroy him from among his people, because he gave his child to be bound to an angel, defiling my holy places and defiling the name of my holy ones.
But if the people of that land overlook that man and hide their eyes from him while he dedicates his child to an angel, and do not kill him,
I will set my face against that man and against his relatives. I will destroy him and all who joined with him to prostitute themselves with angels, removing them from among their people.
If anyone follows mediums and sorcerers, prostituting themselves by following them, I will set my face against that person and destroy him from among his people.
Be holy, for I am the Lord, your holy God.
Keep my commandments and carry them out, for I am the Lord God, who makes you holy.
If a man speaks evil against his father or his mother, he shall certainly be put to death. He has spoken evil against his father or his mother; he is guilty.

If a man commits adultery with another man's wife, or if anyone commits adultery with his neighbor's wife, both the man who committed adultery and the woman who committed adultery must be put to death.
If anyone sleeps with his father's wife, he has exposed his father's nakedness. Both of them must be put to death; they are guilty.
If anyone sleeps with his son's wife, both of them must be put to death, because they have committed a sin and are guilty.
If anyone sleeps with a male as with a woman, both of them have done something unclean. They must be put to death; they are guilty.
If anyone takes a woman together with her mother, that is a sin. They must burn him and the women with fire, so that sin does not come upon you.
Anyone who sleeps with an animal must be put to death, and you must kill the animal too.
And if a woman approaches an animal to have it lie with her, kill both the woman and the animal. Both must be put to death; they are guilty.

If someone lies with his sister, whether his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and sees her nakedness, and she sees his nakedness, it is a disgrace. They must be cut off before the members of their family, because he has uncovered his sister's nakedness, and they will bear their guilt.
If a man sleeps with a menstruating woman and exposes her nakedness, he has exposed her flow, and she has exposed the discharge of her blood. Both of them must be cut off from their people.
Do not expose the nakedness of your father's sister or your mother's sister, because if they expose the nakedness of their relative, they will bear their sin.
Anyone who sleeps with his relative's wife has exposed his relative's nakedness. They must die childless.
A man who sleeps with his brother's wife has exposed his brother's nakedness. They will die childless.
Keep all my commandments and carry them out, so that the land into which I am bringing you to live will not reject you.
Do not follow the customs of the nations whom I drive out from among you, because they did all these things, and I detested them.
I said to you, 'You will inherit their land, and I will give it to you to possess, a land flowing with milk and honey.' I am the Lord your God, who separated you from all the nations.

Distinguish for yourselves between unclean animals and clean animals, and between clean birds and unclean birds. Do not make yourselves unclean through animals, birds, or anything that moves on the earth which I have set apart for you as unclean.
You must be holy to me, because I, the Lord your God, am holy. I separated you from all the nations so that you would belong to me.
If a woman or a man is a diviner or a sorcerer, they must be put to death. Stone them with stones, because they are guilty.
The Lord said to Moses, 'Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and tell them not to defile themselves through a dead person among their people.'
Except for those of their household who are close to them, whether their father, their mother, their sons, their daughters, or his brother;
Or for [?] his sister, or for a virgin who is closely related to him and has not had a husband; for these they may make themselves unclean.
He must not defile himself at that time through someone among his people, and he must not become unclean.
Do not shave your heads for someone who has died. Do not shave the hair of your faces, and do not cut your flesh.
They must be holy to their God and must not profane the name of their God, because they present the sacrifice to the Lord, the offering to their God. They must be holy.
They must not marry a prostitute or a defiled woman, nor a woman whom her husband has sent away, because the priest is holy to the Lord his God.
You must sanctify him, because he presents the offering to the Lord your God. He must be holy, because I, the Lord who sanctifies them, am holy.
If the daughter of a priest defiles her father's name through prostitution, they shall disgrace her and burn her with fire.
The priest who is greater than his brothers, on whose head they have poured the blessed oil, and who has been consecrated to wear the sacred garments, must not shave his head or tear his clothes.
He must not go in where any dead person is, not even his father or his mother, so that he does not become defiled.
He must not leave the sanctuary or profane the holy name of his God, because the holy anointing oil of his God is upon him. For I am the Lord.
He shall take as his wife a virgin from his own clan.
But he shall not marry a widow, a divorced woman, a defiled woman, or a prostitute. Instead, he shall take as his wife a virgin from his own clan.
He shall not defile his offspring among his people, for I am the Lord who makes him holy.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Tell Aaron and say to him: Throughout your generations, if any man from your clan has [?] upon him and is not unblemished, he shall not enter to present his offering to his God.
No man who is not unblemished shall enter: neither a blind man, nor a lame man, nor one whose back is short, nor one whose ear is cut off;
nor a man with a fracture in his hand or a broken foot;
nor a hunchback, nor one with a deformity, nor one whose eyes are clouded, nor a man with scabs, nor one with a skin eruption upon him, nor one who has only one testicle.

No descendant of Aaron the priest who has a blemish and is not clean may approach to bring a sacrifice to the LORD, because he is not clean. He must not enter or approach to present the offering of his God.
He may, however, eat the offerings of his God, both the most holy and the holy.
But he shall not enter near the curtain or approach the altar, because he is not unblemished, so that he does not defile the holy things of his God. For I am the Lord who makes them holy.
Moses told this to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Tell Aaron and his sons to keep away from the holy things of the Israelites and not to defile my holy name through anything they consecrate to me. I am the Lord.

This is what I say to them: Throughout your generations, anyone among all your descendants who enters among the holy things that the Israelites consecrate to the Lord while he has uncleanness upon him—that person shall be cut off from me. For I am the Lord.

If any man among Aaron’s descendants has leprosy or a discharge of semen, he shall not eat any of the holy things until he becomes clean. The same applies to anyone who touches any uncleanness from a dead body, or a man from whom semen has come out;
or anyone who touches any creeping thing that makes him unclean, anything unclean among all unclean things.
The person who touches it is unclean until evening and shall not eat any of the holy things unless he has washed his body with water.
Once the sun has set, he is clean, and then he may eat the holy things, because they are his food.
You shall not eat an animal that has died or has been eaten by a wild beast, so that you do not become unclean through it. For I am the Lord.
Keep my commandment so that you do not incur sin because of it and do not die because of it if they become unclean through it. I am the Lord who makes them holy.
No one from another clan shall eat any of the holy things. Neither a priest’s lodger nor his hired worker shall eat any of the holy things.
But if a priest acquires a person purchased with his gold, that person may eat, because it is his food. Those born in his house may also eat; it is their food.
If the daughter of a priest marries a man from another clan, she shall not eat any of the holy tithes.

If a priest’s daughter becomes a widow and her husband has left her, let her return to her father’s house as when she was young, and let her eat her father’s food. But no one from another clan shall eat any of it.
If anyone unknowingly eats any of the holy things, he shall add a fifth to it and give the holy thing to the priest.
They must not profane the sacred offerings of the Israelites that they bring to the Lord.
They will incur guilt requiring atonement because they have eaten their sacred offerings, for I am the Lord who makes them holy.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:

Tell Aaron, his sons, and the whole congregation of the Israelites, and say to them: Any man among the Israelites or among the foreigners living in Israel who brings his offering for any vow they have made or anything they have freely decided to give—all that they bring to the Lord—
must choose from the best: an unblemished male from the cattle, sheep, or goats.
They must not bring anything with a defect to the Lord, for it will not be accepted on your behalf.
If anyone brings a peace offering to the Lord in fulfillment of a vow or of his own free will, from the cattle or sheep, it must be unblemished to be accepted on their behalf, with no defect at all.
They must not bring to the Lord an animal that is blind, broken, has a cut tongue, has raw skin, has swellings, or has scabies. Do not offer any of these as an offering on the Lord’s altar.
A cow or sheep with a cut ear or a cut tail you may mark and keep as your own livestock, but it will not be accepted on your behalf for your vow.
They must not bring to the Lord an animal with crushed, squeezed, cut, or torn-out testicles. Nor must you do this in your land.
Nor may you receive any of these from someone of foreign descent and bring it as an offering to your God, for it is damaged and has a defect. It will not be accepted on your behalf.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:

When a cow, ewe, or female goat gives birth, its young must remain with its mother for seven days. On the eighth day and afterward, it will be accepted on your behalf as a sacrificial offering to the Lord.
Do not slaughter a cow or ewe together with its young on the same day.
If you offer the Lord a sacrifice in fulfillment of your vow of rejoicing, offer it to him so that it will be accepted on your behalf.
They must eat it that same day and leave none of its meat until morning, for I am the Lord.
Keep my commandments and carry them out, for I am the Lord.
Do not profane my holy name. I will be sanctified among the children of Israel, for I am the LORD who sanctifies them.
I brought them out of the land of Egypt so that I might be your God. I am the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Tell the Israelites and say to them: The Lord’s festivals, which you designate by holy names—these are my festivals.
For six days you shall do your work, but the seventh day is a Sabbath, a holy rest designated for the Lord. You must do no work at all, for it is the Lord’s Sabbath wherever you live.
These are the LORD's festivals, which you have proclaimed by holy names in your allotted divisions.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, in the middle of the night, is the Lord’s Passover.
On the fifteenth day of this month is the Lord’s Festival of Unleavened Bread. Eat unleavened bread for seven days.
The first day shall be proclaimed holy for you. You must not do any work of service.
Bring sacrifices to the LORD for seven days. On the seventh day a holy occasion shall be proclaimed for you. You must not do any work of service.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Tell the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land that I am giving you and reap its harvest, bring a sheaf from the first of your harvest to the priest.
The priest shall present that sheaf before the Lord so that you may be accepted. The priest shall present it on the day after the first day.
On the day when you bring that sheaf, offer an unblemished lamb one year old as a sacrifice to the LORD.
Its grain offering shall be two-tenths of a measure of fine flour mixed with oil, an offering to the Lord as a pleasing aroma to the Lord. Its drink offering shall be a quarter of a hin of wine.

On the day when you bring an offering to your God, you shall not eat new bread or roasted grain until you have brought the offering to your God that day. This shall be a lasting statute for you throughout your generations, wherever you live.
You shall count from the day after the Sabbath, from the day when you brought the sheaf presented as an offering. You shall count seven complete Sabbaths.
You shall count fifty days, up to the day after the last Sabbath, and bring a new offering to the Lord from your land.

You shall bring two loaves of bread to be presented as an offering. Each loaf shall be made from two-tenths of a measure of fine flour. You shall bake them with leaven as the firstfruits of your grain for the Lord.

Along with that bread, bring seven lambs, each one year old, one bull from the herd, and two rams, without blemish. They shall be an offering to the LORD, together with their grain offerings and their drink offerings, a sacrifice of pleasing aroma to the LORD.
Offer one male goat as a sin offering and two year-old lambs as a peace offering, together with that bread of the firstfruits.
The priest shall bring it with that bread of the firstfruits and present it before the Lord together with those two lambs. It is holy to the Lord and shall belong to the priest who presented it.
Proclaim this day as holy; it shall be called holy for you. You shall do no ordinary work on it. This shall be a lasting statute for you throughout your generations, wherever you are.

When you reap the harvest of your land, do not finish reaping everything. Do not gather what remains in your fields as you reap. Leave it for the poor and the resident foreigner, for I am the LORD your God.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Tell the Israelites and say to them: In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall have a day of rest, a memorial marked by trumpet blasts, a holy assembly for the Lord.
You shall do no ordinary work, and you shall bring an offering to the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
The tenth day of the seventh month is the Day of Atonement. It shall be called holy for you. You shall humble yourselves and bring an offering to the Lord.
You shall do no ordinary work on that day, because it is your Day of Atonement, on which atonement is made for you before the Lord your God.
Anyone who does not humble themselves on that day shall be cut off from their people.
Anyone who does work on that day must be wiped out from among their people.
You shall do no work on it. This shall be a lasting statute for you throughout your generations, wherever you are.

It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you. You shall humble yourselves. From the evening of the ninth day of the month until the evening of the tenth day of the month, you shall observe your Sabbath rest.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Tell the Israelites and say to them: On the fifteenth day of that month begins the Festival of Shelters, lasting seven days for the Lord.
The first day shall be called holy. You shall do no ordinary work.

For seven days you shall bring sacrifices to the LORD. The eighth day shall be proclaimed holy for you, and you shall bring a sacrifice to the LORD, for it is a closing assembly. You must not do any work of service.

These are the Lord’s festivals, which you shall proclaim as holy assemblies, at which gifts shall be brought to the Lord, together with offerings, their sacrifices, and the drink offerings for each day.
These are in addition to the LORD's Sabbaths, your gifts, all your vowed offerings, and your freewill offerings that you bring to the LORD.

On the fifteenth day of that seventh month, when you have finished gathering the harvest of your land, you shall celebrate a festival for the Lord for seven days. The first day is a day of rest, and the eighth day is also a day of rest.

On the first day, take for yourselves fruit from beautiful trees, shoots of plants and date palms, branches from leafy trees and willows, and branches of chaste trees from the river. Rejoice before the LORD your God for seven days every year.
It shall be a lasting statute for you throughout your generations that you celebrate the festival in the seventh month.
You shall live in shelters for seven days. Everyone native-born in Israel shall live in shelters.
So that your generations may see that I made the Israelites live in shelters when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
Moses told the Israelites about the festivals of the Lord God.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:
Command the Israelites to bring you pure, beaten olive oil for lighting, so that you may keep a lamp burning at all times.

Outside the curtain of the tent of testimony, Aaron and his sons shall keep it burning before the LORD continually, from evening until morning. This shall be an everlasting statute for you throughout your generations.
Light the lamp on the pure lampstand before the LORD until morning.
Take fine flour and make twelve loaves. Each loaf shall contain two tenths.
Arrange them in stacks, with six loaves in each stack, on the clean table before the LORD.
Place pure frankincense and salt with them, and the bread shall be set before the LORD as a memorial.
On the Sabbath day you shall arrange it before the LORD continually on behalf of the children of Israel. It is an everlasting statute.
It shall belong to Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat it in a holy place, because it is most holy for him among the offerings made to the LORD. This is an everlasting statute.
The son of an Israelite woman, whose father was Egyptian, went out among the Israelites. The son of the Israelite woman and an Israelite man quarreled in the camp.
The son of that Israelite woman uttered the name of the LORD and cursed. They brought him to Moses. His mother's name was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, from the tribe of Dan.
He put him in custody until he could judge him according to the LORD's command.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:
Take the one who cursed outside the camp. Let everyone who heard him put their hands on his head, and let the whole congregation stone him.
Tell the Israelites and say to them: If anyone curses God, he shall be guilty of sin.

For whoever utters the name of the LORD must be put to death. Let the whole congregation stone him. Whether a foreign resident or a native-born person, if he utters the name of the LORD, he shall die.
Anyone who kills any human being shall be put to death.
But if he kills an animal, he shall make restitution, life for life.
If anyone injures another person, let them do to him just as he did to the other person.
Fracture for fracture, eye for eye, and tooth for tooth. Just as he injured another person, do the same to him.
Anyone who strikes a person and kills him must be put to death.
There shall be one judgment for both the foreign resident and the native-born person, for I am the LORD your God.
Moses spoke to the Israelites, and they took the one who had blasphemed outside the camp. The whole congregation stoned him. The Israelites did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai and said to him:
Tell the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land that I am giving you, the land that I am giving you shall rest and observe a Sabbath for the LORD.
For six years you shall sow your field, and for six years you shall prune your vineyard and gather its fruit.
But in the seventh year there shall be a Sabbath of rest for the land, and it shall keep a Sabbath to the LORD. You must not sow your field or prune your vineyard.
You shall not reap what grows by itself in your field, nor shall you gather the consecrated grapes that year, for it is a rest for the land.
The produce of the land during its Sabbath shall be food for you, your male servant, your female servant, your hired worker, and the foreign resident who lives with you;
And for your livestock and the wild animals in your land. All its produce shall be food for you.

Count for yourself seven periods of rest, seven times seven years. These shall make seven sabbaths for you, at which you shall make a proclamation with a trumpet throughout all your land, every forty-nine years.
In the seventh month, on the Day of Atonement, you shall make a proclamation with a trumpet throughout all your land.

Consecrate that fiftieth year, the whole year, and proclaim release throughout all your land to everyone who lives in it, for it is a year of release. It shall be a sign for you. Everyone shall return to his property, and everyone shall go to his own town.

The sign of release. That fiftieth year shall be for you a year of release throughout the whole year. You shall not sow or reap, except what grows by itself, and you shall not gather what has been consecrated during it.
For it is a sign of release, and it shall be holy to you. Eat the grain that comes from the open fields.
In that year marked by release, everyone shall return to his property.
If anyone sells to his neighbor, or if anyone buys from his neighbor, he shall not wrong his neighbor.
After the year of the sign, he shall sell to his neighbor, and he shall pay you according to the seasons when grain is sown in that year.

In proportion to the greater number of those years, he shall increase the purchase price; and as those years decrease, he shall reduce the price of his sale. He shall pay you according to the seasons when grain is sown.
No one shall wrong his neighbor. Fear the Lord your God, for I am the Lord your God.
Carry out all my ordinances and all my judgments. Observe them and carry them out, and you shall live securely in your land.
The land shall give you its produce, and you shall eat and be satisfied and live securely in it.
If you say, “What shall we eat in that seventh year, if we do not sow and do not gather our grain?”
I will send you my blessing in the sixth year, and it shall produce its yield, enough grain for three years.
You shall sow some of it in the eighth year, and you shall eat that stored grain until the ninth year. Until its grain comes in, you shall eat the old grain kept in storage.
The land shall not be sold permanently, for the land is mine, and you are foreigners and temporary residents before me.
Throughout the territory of your land, wherever your authority extends, you shall allow the land to be redeemed.
If your fellow who lives beside you becomes poor and sells you his land, and afterward a close relative belonging to his family comes, he shall redeem what his brother sold.
If someone has no one to redeem his property, but afterward acquires the means and has enough to redeem it,
they shall count for him the years since he sold it. He shall pay the corresponding amount to the man to whom he sold it, and his fields shall return to him.
But if he does not acquire enough to repay him, his fields shall belong to the buyer until the year of release. They shall be released in the year of release, and he shall recover his fields.
If someone sells his house in a town that has a wall, he shall have until the days of that year are completed to redeem it, and it may be redeemed.

But if that whole year is completed and he has not redeemed it, that house shall belong permanently to the buyer. That house in the walled town shall be secured to him and shall belong to his descendants’ descendants. They shall not take it from him at the release.
But houses in a town that has no wall around it shall be redeemed like fields in the countryside. They may be redeemed at any time, and at the release they shall be returned.
As for the towns of the Levites, their houses within their towns may be redeemed at any time, and they shall be redeemed for the Levites.

Everything redeemed from the Levites, including houses within their towns that became their owners’ property through sale, shall be returned at the release within their territory. For the houses of their towns are the Levites’ [?], to belong to them among the Israelites.
The fields within the boundaries of their towns shall not be sold, for they are their territory forever.
If your neighbor who lives with you becomes poor and cannot support himself among you, support him as you would a foreigner or a temporary resident, so that your neighbor may live with you.
Do not take interest from him, not even if he has accumulated much [?]. Fear your God, for I am the Lord, and let your neighbor live with you.
Do not lend him your gold at interest, and do not charge him interest on your grain.
For I am the Lord, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
If your fellow countryman becomes poor and is sold to you, he must not serve you as a slave.
Instead, he must be with you as a hired worker and as a foreign resident. He must serve you until the year of release.
In the year of release, he and his children with him must go free. He must return to his relatives and his territory and go back to his homeland.
For they are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. They must not be sold as a slave is sold.
Do not oppress him with hard labor, but fear the Lord your God.
As for male and female slaves, you may acquire them from the nations around you, buying male and female slaves from among them.
You may also buy them from among the children of those who reside with you and from all their families who live in your land. They may become your property.
You may distribute them among your children, and they may be your property forever. But among your brothers, the Israelites, no one must oppress another with hard labor.
But if that resident alien, or that foreigner living with you, acquires wealth, and his family says to you, ‘Sell him to me, to this resident alien or to that foreigner living with you,’
after you have sold him to them, even if you sell him to a relative of that resident alien, one of his relatives must redeem him.

One of his father's brothers or a son of his father's brother may redeem him. Someone from his family, his own flesh and blood, or his clan may redeem him. If he himself acquires the means, he may redeem himself.

They must calculate for his purchaser the time from the year in which he bought him until the year of release. They must assess his purchase money according to the daily rate of a hired worker for the years he is with him.
If it exceeds eight years, he must pay his redemption price out of his purchase money.
But if only a few years remain until the year of release, they must calculate his years for him, and he must pay his redemption price,
according to the wages of a hired worker who is with him from year to year, and not according to each year in which he made him toil for him in his presence [?].
If he is not redeemed in this way, he must go free from him in the year of release, together with his children.
For the Israelites are my servants, whom I brought out of Egypt, and I am the Lord your God.
Do not make for yourselves objects fashioned by human hands or carved images. Do not set up a stone monument in your land to bow down to it, for I am the Lord your God.
Keep my Sabbaths and revere my holy places, for I am the Lord.
If you walk according to my commandments, keep my judgments, and carry them out;
I will give you rain in its season. The land will yield its crops, and the trees of the countryside will yield their fruit.
The harvest will last until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest will last until sowing time. You will eat your food to the full and live securely in your land.
I will give you peace in your land. You will sleep, and no one will frighten you. I will eliminate the wild animals from your country.
You will kill your enemies, and they will die before you.
Five of you will put a hundred to flight, and a hundred of you will put ten thousand to flight. Your enemies will fall before you by the sword.
I will look favorably upon you, make you grow and multiply, and establish my covenant with you.
You will eat the old harvest and harvests from earlier years, and you will bring out the old to bring in the new.
I will establish my dwelling among you, and my soul will not detest you.
I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be my people.
For I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt when you were slaves. I broke your shackles and brought you out openly.
But if you do not listen to me and do not carry out my commandments,
but reject them, and your souls resent my judgments, so that you do not carry out all my commandments and abandon my ordinances,

I too will do the same to you: I will bring evil upon you, scabs and wasting disease, which will dim your eyes and make your lives waste away. You shall sow your seed in vain, and your enemies shall eat what you produce.
I will set my face against you, and you shall fall before your enemies. Those who hate you shall drive you away, and you shall flee when no one is pursuing you.
and if even after this you do not listen to me, I will increase your punishment sevenfold because of your sins.
I will break the strength of your pride and make your sky like iron and your earth like bronze.
Your strength will be spent in vain. The earth will not give you its crops, and the trees of the countryside will not give you their fruit.
If after this you still act perversely and refuse to listen to me, I will add seven punishments for you, according to your sins.
I will send vicious wild beasts of the earth against you. They will devour you and destroy your livestock, leave only a few of you, and make your roads deserted.
If even after this you do not fear, but act perversely toward me,
I too will act perversely toward you in anger, and I myself will kill you sevenfold because of your sins.

I will bring a sword upon you that will pursue you and exact vengeance from you for my covenant. You shall flee into your cities, and I will send death upon you, and you shall fall into the hands of your enemies.
When I afflict you with a shortage of the food that sustains you, ten women will bake your bread in one oven and give you your bread by weight. You will eat but will not be satisfied.
If even after this you do not listen to me, but act perversely toward me,
I too will act perversely toward you in anger, and I myself will punish you sevenfold according to your sins.
You will eat the flesh of your sons and eat the flesh of your daughters.
I will destroy your images and uproot the wooden objects made by your hands. I will scatter your corpses over the images of your gods, and I will loathe you.
I will make your cities a ruin and destroy your sanctuaries, and I will not smell the fragrance of your sacrifices.
I myself will make your land desolate, and your enemies who live in it will be astonished at it.
I will scatter you among the nations and destroy you with the sword wherever you go. Your land shall become a wilderness, and your cities shall become a ruin.

Then the land will enjoy its Sabbaths throughout all the days of its desolation, while you are in the land of your enemies. Then the land will rest and enjoy its Sabbaths throughout all the days of its desolation.
It will rest as it did not rest during your Sabbaths when you were living in it.

As for those of you who remain, I will bring terror into their hearts in the land of their enemies. They shall be frightened by the sound of a rustling leaf and flee as someone flees from an enemy. They shall fall when no one is pursuing them.
They will stumble over one another as in battle, though no one is pursuing them, and you will not be able to stand against your enemies.
You will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will swallow you up.
Those of you who remain will waste away because of their sins, and because of the sins of their fathers they will wither away in the land of their enemies.
They will acknowledge their sins and the sins of their fathers: how they rejected me and offended me, and how they acted perversely before me.
I too acted against them in anger, and I will destroy them in the land of their enemies. Then their uncircumcised hearts will be ashamed, and then they will make amends for their sins.
I will remember my covenant with Jacob, and my covenant with Isaac, and my covenant with Abraham; and I will also remember the land.

The land will be abandoned by them. Then the land will receive its Sabbaths while it lies desolate because of them. They too will bear the punishment for their sins, because they rejected my judgments and detested my commandments.
Yet while they were in the land of their enemies, I did not reject them or detest them so as to destroy them because they had abandoned my covenant with them, for I am the Lord their God.
I will remember their former covenant, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, in the sight of the nations, to be their God. I am the Lord.
These are the commandments, judgments, and laws that the Lord established between himself and the Israelites on Mount Sinai through Moses.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: If a man makes a vow to the Lord as a payment for redeeming himself;
The assessed value of a male from twenty to sixty years old shall be fifty silver didrachmas, according to the sanctuary weight.
For a female, her assessed value shall be thirty didrachmas.
For someone from five to twenty years old, the assessed value shall be twenty didrachmas for a male and ten didrachmas for a female.
If the person is from one month to five years old, the assessed value for a male shall be five silver didrachmas, and for a female three silver didrachmas.
For someone sixty years old or more, the assessed value shall be fifteen silver didrachmas for a male and ten didrachmas for a female.

If he is too poor to meet the assessed value, he shall stand before the priest, and the priest shall assess his value according to what he has available. The priest shall assess his value according to what the person who made the vow can afford.
If it is an animal of a kind that may be brought as an offering to the Lord, whatever he brings from it to the Lord shall be holy.
He shall not exchange a good one for a bad one, or a bad one for a good one. If he does exchange one animal for another of its kind, both it and its substitute shall be holy.
If it is any unclean animal, of a kind from which no offering may be brought to the Lord, you shall present that animal before the priest.
The priest shall assess its value according to whether it is good or bad. Whatever value the priest assesses shall stand.
If he does redeem it, he shall add one-fifth to its assessed value.
If a man vows his house to the Lord and consecrates it, the priest shall assess its value according to whether it is good or bad. Whatever value the priest assesses shall stand.
If the person who made the vow redeems his house, he shall add one-fifth to the gold of its assessed value, and it shall return to him.
If a man vows to the Lord some of the fields that belong to him, their value shall be set according to the amount of seed sown in them: fifty pieces of silver for a kor-measure of barley.
If he vows his field from the year of Jubilee, its value shall be according to the assessment.

If he vows his field in a year after the Jubilee, the priest shall calculate its gold payment for him according to the years remaining until the year of Jubilee, and shall deduct that amount from its assessed value.
If the man who vowed his field redeems it himself, he shall add one-fifth to its assessed value in gold, and his field shall return to him.
If, after redeeming his field, he sells it to another man, he shall not redeem it again.

But his field shall be holy and honored, belonging to the Lord. In the year of release it shall pass out of his possession and shall not return to him. Like land set apart, it shall belong to the priest within his territory.
If he vows to the Lord some land that he purchased, which is not part of his inherited property:
The priest shall calculate for him the full assessed value from the year of release, and on that day he shall give its assessed value as his vowed offering to the Lord.
In the year of Jubilee, that field shall return to the man from whom it was purchased, because it is his inherited property and his land.
Every valuation shall be according to the sanctuary weight: twenty obols to one didrachm.
Every firstborn born among your livestock belongs to the Lord, and no one may exchange it. Whether an ox or a sheep, it belongs to the Lord.

If it is an unclean animal, he may redeem it at its assessed value, adding one-fifth to it, and it shall belong to him. If he does not redeem it, it shall be sold at its assessed value. No devoted offering that anyone dedicates to the Lord from anything he owns—whether a person, an animal, or a field belonging to him—may be sold or redeemed.
Every devoted offering is most holy to the Lord.
Every person devoted as an offering, whoever he may be, shall not be redeemed until he dies.
Every tithe of the land, whether from the seed of the land or from the fruit of a tree, belongs to the Lord; it is holy to the Lord.
If anyone redeems his tithe, he shall add one-fifth to it.
Every tithe of cattle and sheep, and everything driven under the rod to be counted, is holy, and its tithe belongs to the Lord.
They shall not exchange a good one for a bad one, or a bad one for a good one. If anyone does exchange it, its substitute is holy and shall not be redeemed.
This is the commandment that the Lord gave Moses on Mount Sinai to tell the Israelites.
